public_payload.normalized_proposition: Large language models are not a profitable business.

statement.excerpt: It’s becoming increasingly apparent that Large Language Models are not a profitable business.
statement.document_title: This Is How Much Anthropic and Cursor Spend On Amazon Web Services

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading concerns the current profitability of developing and selling LLM services, especially the major standalone developers discussed in context.
Profitability means revenue exceeding full operating costs, including research and model development. Positive gross margin alone is insufficient.
This is not read as a prediction that LLMs can never become profitable.
Because the sentence names no reporting period, use the first half of 2025, the latest completed financial reporting period identified in contemporaneous public reporting before the post.
The statement specifies no accounting basis. The contract therefore records unknown rather than assigning GAAP, non-GAAP, or an estimated basis.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable financial records show that the major LLM-development businesses were operating at a loss after full operating costs during the target period, with enough coverage to justify the generalization.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records show that the major LLM-development businesses generally earned operating profits after full operating costs during the target period. Isolated profitable products would qualify the generalization but would not necessarily refute its ordinary reading.
